root_cause.text: ieee80211_ml_reconfiguration in mac80211 trusted the 4-bit link_id parsed from the ML Reconfiguration element and used it to index the fixed-size link_removal_timeout[]/removed_links state without validating that the value fit within IEEE80211_MLD_MAX_NUM_LINKS, allowing link_id 15 to go out of bounds.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message explicitly states “link_id is taken from the ML Reconfiguration element (control & 0x000f), so it can be 0..15” while “link_removal_timeout[] has IEEE80211_MLD_MAX_NUM_LINKS (15) elements, so index 15 is out-of-bounds,” and the patch fixes this by adding `if (link_id >= IEEE80211_MLD_MAX_NUM_LINKS) continue;` in `ieee80211_ml_reconfiguration`.

agent_logs.root_cause_candidate: ieee80211_ml_reconfiguration in mac80211 trusted the 4-bit link_id parsed from the ML Reconfiguration element and used it to index the fixed-size link_removal_timeout[]/removed_links state without validating that the value fit within IEEE80211_MLD_MAX_NUM_LINKS, allowing link_id 15 to go out of bounds.
agent_logs.evidence_points: The commit message explicitly states “link_id is taken from the ML Reconfiguration element (control & 0x000f), so it can be 0..15” while “link_removal_timeout[] has IEEE80211_MLD_MAX_NUM_LINKS (15) elements, so index 15 is out-of-bounds,” and the patch fixes this by adding `if (link_id >= IEEE80211_MLD_MAX_NUM_LINKS) continue;` in `ieee80211_ml_reconfiguration`.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add a bounds check for link_id in ML reconfiguration to skip invalid entries before updating removed_links.
intent_record.what: A new conditional check was added after extracting link_id from prof->control: if link_id is greater than or equal to IEEE80211_MLD_MAX_NUM_LINKS, the loop skips that entry with continue before executing removed_links |= BIT(link_id).
intent_record.how: At runtime, this prevents processing invalid link IDs and avoids setting a bit using an out-of-range index, which could otherwise lead to incorrect removed_links state or undefined behavior from an invalid BIT(link_id) operation.

grouping_result.intent: Add a bounds check for link_id in ML reconfiguration to skip invalid entries before updating removed_links.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly addresses the root cause by validating link_id bounds in ML reconfiguration before using it to update removed_links, preventing out-of-bounds access from invalid 4-bit link_id values.

candidates.rationale: This uses the unvalidated 4-bit link_id directly in a bit operation updating removed_links. If link_id is 15 and exceeds IEEE80211_MLD_MAX_NUM_LINKS, it causes out-of-bounds/invalid state handling exactly as described in the root cause.
This extracts the attacker-controlled link_id from the ML Reconfiguration element without validating it against IEEE80211_MLD_MAX_NUM_LINKS, enabling the later unsafe use.

vuln_statements.explanation: This statement performs the unsafe use of the attacker-controlled link_id without validating that it is less than IEEE80211_MLD_MAX_NUM_LINKS. A parsed value such as 15 can therefore be applied to fixed-size link state, matching the out-of-bounds/invalid state update described in the root cause.

This statement extracts the 4-bit link_id from the received ML Reconfiguration element. Because no subsequent bounds validation was performed before using link_id for link state updates, it is the source of the untrusted index value that triggers the vulnerability.

commit 8eb8dd2ffbbb6b0b8843b66754ee9f129f1b2d6c
Author: Ilan Peer <ilan.peer@intel.com>
Date:   Sun Jun 18 21:49:55 2023 +0300

    wifi: mac80211: Support link removal using Reconfiguration ML element
    
    Add support for handling link removal indicated by the
    Reconfiguration Multi-Link element.
    
    Signed-off-by: Ilan Peer <ilan.peer@intel.com>
    Signed-off-by: Gregory Greenman <gregory.greenman@intel.com>
    Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/20230618214436.d8a046dc0c1a.I4dcf794d
bic_trace_step.reason: The snippet fully shows the relevant parsing and indexing logic in `ieee80211_ml_reconfiguration()`, so it is sufficient to determine the issue. The vulnerable construct is present: `link_id = control & IEEE80211_MLE_STA_RECONF_CONTROL_LINK_ID;` takes the parsed 4-bit link ID directly from the element, and then uses it without validating it against `IEEE80211_MLD_MAX_NUM_LINKS`. Specifically, the code does `removed_links |= BIT(link_id);` and later `link_removal_timeout[link_id] = le16_to_cpu(*(__le16 *)pos);` where `link_removal_timeout` is declared as `u16 link_removal_timeout[IEEE80211_MLD_MAX_NUM_LINKS] = {};`. If `link_id` is 15 while `IEEE80211_MLD_MAX_NUM_LINKS` is smaller, this is an out-of-bounds array write. There is no check such as `if (link_id >= IEEE80211_MLD_MAX_NUM_LINKS) ...` before the bitmap/array access. The later loop `for_each_set_bit(link_id, &removed_links, IEEE80211_MLD_MAX_NUM_LINKS)` only iterates valid indices afterward, but it does not prevent the earlier out-of-bounds write. Therefore the bug is present and the fix is not yet in this version.
